Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. Before we move forward with signature, our DPO needs a short, auditable statement on three items for the DPA amendment:

1) Production request/response logs: canonical retention period, where they are stored, and how deletion is performed on request.
2) Backups and snapshots: frequency, retention, geo-replication behavior, and guarantees around deletion (including physical media scrub).
3) Prompt retention / KV cache behavior: are prompts persisted, for how long, and what guarantees do you provide for purging prompt text and derived embeddings?

We're a HIPAA-regulated customer and need to confirm that any PII ingested via API can be deleted from all storage tiers within a contractual window. Can you provide a high-level timeline (logical deletion vs physical scrub) and attach any SOC 2 / evidence you can share?

Appreciate a concise response we can attach to the DPA amendment (we prefer short bullets).

Hi Alex / Laura,

Below are concise, auditable bullets you can attach to the DPA amendment. I'm also attaching the latest SOC 2 Type II summary and a short excerpt from our retention runbook.

- Request/response logs: By default, request/response logs (API request metadata and runtime traces) are retained for 90 days in encrypted object storage (AES-256). Logical deletion (marking records as deleted and removing indexes) occurs within 4 hours of a validated deletion request. Full propagation across active replicas and caches completes within up to 72 hours; we log the deletion event and provide a signed confirmation to the customer.

- Backups & snapshots: Automated snapshots are taken daily and kept for 30 days in our primary region; weekly snapshots are retained for 90 days. Backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256 and can be configured to use customer-managed KMS keys. Geo-replication to our secondary region is asynchronous; deletion requests remove object pointers immediately and we schedule physical media scrub during the next vendor retention cycle — physical media overwrite/scrub is completed within 90 days.

- Prompts, KV cache & derived artifacts: By default, prompt text and ephemeral caches are held in a short-lived store for operational debugging and quality monitoring. Default retention for prompt text is 7 days; embeddings and derived vectors are retained for 30 days unless the customer opts into longer retention. For HIPAA customers who require prompt non-retention, we offer a configuration that disables prompt persistence and KV caching for a tenant, in which case prompts are not written to persistent storage. On deletion requests we remove prompt artifacts and derived vectors from primary stores within 24 hours and from auxiliary caches/analytics stores within 72 hours.

If HealthRight requires tighter contractual SLAs (e.g., 48-hour full scrub across geo replicas), we can offer a DPA amendment and implementation plan (DocuSign link below).

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf, retention_runbook_excerpt.pdf, backup_lifecycle_diagram.png

Let me know if you want any of the bullets shortened for legal.

—Monica

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the specificity — we can meet HealthRight halfway. Proposed (summary):

- Deletion SLA: full logical deletion across active replicas and cache eviction guaranteed within 48 hours for production tenants that opt into our "expedited-deletion" amendment (this will be an opt-in addendum to the DPA).
- Physical media scrub: committed within 75 days for expedited-deletion customers; standard customers remain at 90 days.
- Third-party cold storage: our deletion workflow will remove object pointers and issue a deletion request to third-party providers as part of the same workflow; we will include a clause that we will pursue best-effort deletion from third parties and will provide evidence of the outbound deletion request.
- KMS & prompt-non-retention: customer-managed KMS is supported for all persistent stores; for the prompt-non-retention configuration we guarantee no plaintext prompt persistence to long-term storage and no transient plaintext is written to disk with customer-managed keys during processing.
- Deletion certificate: we will provide an automated signed deletion certificate with timestamps (JSON document signed by Redwood's compliance key) and attach it to the customer's audit record.

I've created a short amendment draft and a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://docsend.redwood.com/s/HS-99821-DPA-Amendment. Procurement — please review the amendment and let us know if the expedited option is acceptable as a paid add-on; Laura and Ben, please redline as needed.

Best,
Monica
Customer Solutions — Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
